system.name: MatPlotBench
system.one_liner: Benchmark of 100 human-verified scientific data-visualization cases for LLM agents, from raw data and a query to the expected figure.

content.variant_note: four lettered cases A-D read in three stacked dashed bands (raw data, user query, output figure), so each case is one column of input, request and expected result
content.argues: A visualization agent must turn raw data plus a natural-language query into a specific kind of scientific plot; MatPlotBench cases cover diverse plot types and requirements.
content.subject: Four benchmark cases, each a raw data table, a user query and the expected output plot, in three banded rows.

encoding.color_means: Band colour tells the kind of content (green = raw data, yellow = user query, indigo = output figure); the letter chips carry one colour per case (A teal, B orange, C salmon, D light blue) repeated in all three bands.
encoding.line_style_means: Dashed frames in the band colour group each band; thin green rules form the tables.
encoding.shape_means: Coloured tab title on a dashed frame = a band; square letter chip = a case; ruled grid = data table; cream card = text; raster tile = output plot.
encoding.marker_means: Letters A-D name the cases and link a table, a query and a plot across the bands.
encoding.emphasis: Colour per band and per case lets the eye follow one case down the bands; the four plots are the largest items.

lessons.what_to_learn: Show benchmark cases as bands by content kind (data, query, expected output) and repeat the same colour-coded letter chip in each band, so every case can be followed across the bands without arrows; crop tables and queries and say so in the caption.
lessons.suits: Benchmark or dataset papers whose items have several parts (inputs, prompt, reference output) and need a quick gallery of what one test case looks like.

evidence: Given the raw data and user queries, the AI agent is expected to generate a figure accordingly.
We only display partial raw data and user queries due to space limitations.

summary: MatPlotAgent is an LLM agent framework for scientific data visualization, and MatPlotBench is the benchmark of 100 human-verified cases built to test it. Figure 1 shows four of its cases in three dashed bands: green Raw Data tables, yellow User Query cards and purple Output Figure plots. Colour-coded letters A to D repeat in every band, so each case reads from data and request to the expected figure: a K-means scatter plot of protein consumption, a phase diagram of water, a 3D waterfall plot and a chord diagram of phone-brand switching. Data tables and queries are cropped, as the caption says.
summary_zh: MatPlotBench 收录 100 个经人工核验的科学数据可视化用例。图 1 以三条虚线带展示四个案例：绿色原始数据表、黄色用户查询、紫色输出图，字母 A–D 在各带中重复，把数据、请求与期望图表对应起来。
notes: Prior label kept (scope-overview, example-gallery). The three dashed bands are counted as panels because each is framed and titled. The Output Figure plots are bitmaps with their own fonts; whether they are reference figures from online sources or were made for the paper is not stated in the figure. The preview has blank space above the figure and the first caption line cut off at its bottom edge.
